exposure: Maternal antenatal exposure to second-hand smoke (SHS)
cohort: The study included 305 mother-infant pairs where the mothers were non-smoking and reported their exposure to second-hand smoke during the 3rd trimester of pregnancy.
finding: Heavy antenatal exposure to second-hand smoke in non-smoking mothers is associated with reduced neonatal head circumference at birth and reduced head circumference gain over the first 6 months of life.
